questions.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 16\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & 10 & 4 \\ 3 & 16 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 16 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one.

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ that is to say, 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 16\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-9 & 8 & -16 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, our matrix is already in a row echelon form.

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ that is to say, 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}.

questions.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are given below. Determine whether $B=\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2},$ where ${a}_{3}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 17\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}={{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 17\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=5 \\ 5{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=17\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 5 \\ 5 & 7 & 17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -8 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the RREF matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=1,$ meaning that

$$
2\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+1\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}={{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 17\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}.
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=2\cdot 1=2.$
